iac.name: OpenTofu Documentation
iac.description: MPL-2.0, Linux Foundation-governed fork of Terraform, accepted into CNCF April 2025. As of mid-2026 it has diverged with OSS features Terraform's binary lacks (state encryption, early variable evaluation, provider for_each iteration, -exclude flag, OCI registry support) — no longer a pure compatibility fork. Independently reported adoption figures (e.g. ~12% of IaC practitioners) are industry-survey estimates, not a primary OpenTofu/CNCF statistic — cite as unverified precision if quoting a number.

platform_engineering.name: Backstage Documentation
platform_engineering.description: Backstage documentation for developer portals and service catalogs. Adoption reality check (2026, industry-reported not official Backstage/CNCF data — treat figures as approximate): internal adoption commonly plateaus around ~10% (proof-of-concept level) unless staffed as a product with 2-3 dedicated engineers for ~12 months; it is a framework requiring in-house TypeScript/React work, not an installable portal; catalog YAML frequently goes stale without automated ingestion; plugin API breaking changes across upgrades are a commonly cited pain point.

sources.name: SLSA v1.2 Specification
sources.notes: Current SLSA build track specification. v1.0 is retired — do not cite the v1.0 page.

sources.name: Sigstore
sources.notes: Project home for cosign, Fulcio, and Rekor — keyless artifact signing infrastructure.

sources.name: DORA 2025 Year in Review
sources.notes: 2025 DORA report retired four-tier clusters (Elite/High/Medium/Low) in favour of seven team archetypes, and expanded four core metrics to five (added rework rate). Central AI finding: AI amplifies existing strengths and weaknesses.

sources.name: DORA Research Publications Index
sources.notes: Canonical list of DORA reports; use to confirm which report (2025 core, 2025 AI Capabilities Model, or 2026 ROI report) a claim belongs to before citing.

sources.name: DORA ROI of AI-assisted Software Development
sources.notes: Newest DORA publication as of July 2026 (published ~April 2026). Introduces the "instability tax" (AI raises delivery instability alongside individual effectiveness) and a J-curve model for AI-adoption ROI. Companion to, not a replacement for, the 2025 core report.

sources.name: CNCF Platform Engineering Maturity Model
sources.notes: Five aspects (Investment, Adoption, Interfaces, Operations, Measurement) x four levels (Provisional, Operationalized, Scalable, Optimizing). Vendor-neutral CNCF TAG App Delivery whitepaper.

sources.name: Kyverno 1.17 Release Blog
sources.notes: CEL-based policy types (ValidatingPolicy, ImageValidatingPolicy) promoted to v1 GA. Legacy ClusterPolicy removal planned ~v1.20 (Oct 2026).

sources.name: SPIFFE Concepts
sources.notes: SPIFFE/SPIRE workload identity concepts — SVIDs, trust domains, federation. The standard for service-to-service identity in 2025-26.
